To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the palliative approach to care is effective in reducing symptoms, improving quality of life, and increasing satisfaction for patients and their families.

the use of palliative care services in the last year of life was associated with a 20% reduction in the risk of death in the first 90 days after admission, but not in the risk of dying within 6 months of admission.
the use of the term “palliative care” is not associated with a higher rate of death, and that the use of palliative care is associated with a higher quality of care and lower costs of care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive palliative care program, with the goal of improving the quality of life for patients with cancer and AIDS.
the development of new and improved methods to control the symptoms of cancer patients.

the following questions: (1) How can we best identify and measure the symptoms of advanced cancer and AIDS? (2) What are the major clinical problems in the care of patients with these conditions? (3) What are the best methods to control the symptoms and problems? and (4) How can we develop effective methods to educate health professionals in the management of these patients?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palliative care is the active total care of patients whose disease is not responsive to curative treatment.
palliative care is a multidisciplinary approach for the management of patients with incurable cancer or AIDS and their families.
palliative care in the cancer patient is a complex process that requires the active participation of the physician, patient, and family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
palliative care in patients with cancer or HIV/AIDS should be provided by a team of health care providers with a wide range of expertise.
the goal of palliative care is to improve the quality of life of patients and their families, and to provide them with comfort and dignity.

palliative care is an approach to patient care that aims to prevent and relieve suffering through early identification and treatment of pain and other problems, whether physical, psychological or spiritual.
